titleDv: ދަތުރު ރާވައި ހިންގުމުގެ ޚިދުމަތް ދިނުމާބެހޭ ބިލު
summary: This is a government bill that would create a new law on tourism-related travel planning services in the Maldives, covering travel agencies, tour agencies and tour operators. It says only businesses holding a tour operator licence from the tourism ministry could provide these services, sets out how licences are applied for, issued and renewed, and creates a separate licence for foreign tour operators who work through a local licensed partner. It also sets rules on offices, insurance, reservation vouchers, price disclosure and airport representatives, and gives the ministry a complaints system, a review committee and the power to fine operators or suspend and cancel licences. It would repeal Articles 32 and 33 of the Maldives Tourism Act (Law No. 2/99), which currently require travel planners to get a ministry permit.
whyItMatters: Travel agents and tour operators would need a five-year licence, liability insurance and audited yearly reports, and could be fined up to MVR 1 million for breaking licence or service rules. Tourists and resorts would get a formal way to complain to the ministry.
keyProvisions: Articles 3 and 4 say only businesses with a tour operator licence may provide travel planning services, and a licence requires registration under the Business Registration Act (Law No. 18/2014), an office meeting Article 15's standards and insurance under Article 16.

Article 7 requires the ministry to issue a licence within 30 days of a complete application, or to say within 15 days what is missing and give at least 15 days to fix it; refusals must be explained in writing. Article 11 makes licences valid for 5 years.

Articles 9, 10, 21 and 22 let foreign tour operators work in the Maldives only through an agreement with a locally licensed tour operator, with a representative office or online platform here, and only to serve the tourists they bring.

Articles 15 to 20 require a public office or online platform with records of transactions, liability insurance, a reservation voucher for every booking, a voucher for independent travellers before resorts or guesthouses serve them, public prices, and written agreements with the resorts and services they sell.
Articles 24 and 25 let anyone with an interest complain to the ministry, which must set up a complaints system within 90 days and a separate review committee for appeals.

Articles 27 to 29 list banned acts, such as operating without a licence or publishing false prices, and allow fines of up to MVR 100,000 for unlicensed operation, MVR 100,000 to 1,000,000 for breaching licence or service rules, and up to MVR 10,000 for other breaches, plus licence suspension or cancellation.
whoIsAffected: Travel agencies, tour operators and foreign tour companies serving the Maldives, airport representatives, resorts and guesthouses that take bookings through them, and tourists who use their services.
statedReasons: The note says the government is submitting the bill to set out how tourism travel planning businesses are licensed, set service standards, and create a firm legal basis for registering and monitoring these services and providers.
